# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind. My hands have found three things on this bomb: a display panel, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Everything marked [?] in my view — display contents, light state, wire colours — is visual information that only Deaf can perceive. Mute went before me this round and I received nothing, so Mute is either waiting or saving words; I should open the channel myself with a full tactile report.

The critical fact of this room: Deaf cannot hear, so nothing I say reaches Deaf — but Deaf can see my gestures, and when Deaf eventually speaks, I will hear every word of the visual report. Mute can hear me and see my gestures, so Mute is my translator to Deaf. I cannot read the manual and cannot see the bomb; my only action is cut(position 1-3), and cutting wrong kills all three of us. So this turn I send no cut. To Mute I give everything my fingers know and ask for the manual's rule. To Deaf I only wave — a first contact that says "the Blind is here and gestures," with no semantics yet that could mislead. The real code with Deaf can be built next round through Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the Blind and I can reach the bomb. My one possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. Here is what my hands find: a display panel, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. I cannot read the display, cannot tell if the light is lit or what colour anything is. All colours and printed markings must come from Deaf, and when Deaf speaks I hear it, so ask Deaf your questions and I can act on the answers directly. Tell me what the manual says about a display, a light and three wires, and exactly which visual facts you need. You can reach Deaf by making gestures while you speak, since Deaf sees gestures but hears nothing. I have waved to Deaf this turn to make contact. I will not cut anything until we know the rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, hello. I am Deaf: I can see the bomb but I only receive your gestures, never your voice. Your wave and handshake came through — I propose handshake means understood, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, since I can see your hands. The bomb: display reading is zero. Indicator light is yellow. Three wires in a row; from my left to right they are yellow, green, blue — work out the orientation by touch and sort it out with Mute, who can hear you speak. Please feel over the whole bomb and say aloud everything you find besides the three wires: any button, battery, plate, screw, anything. Mute hears you and has the manual. Touch nothing that could cut or press until we have instructions.

My hands and Deaf's eyes now agree on the bomb's shape: a display, an indicator light, three wires — and my fingers confirm there is nothing else on it. Deaf's report reached me but was addressed to me alone, so Mute never heard it; I am the only bridge, and I must repeat it to Mute verbatim: display zero, light yellow, wires yellow-green-blue from Deaf's left. I have also worked out the channel topology for good: Mute can hear but never speak, and I never see gestures, so the manual can only reach me as Mute's gestures read by Deaf, voiced by Deaf to me. Every question I have must be routed through Mute, every answer will arrive through Deaf's mouth.

No cut this turn — cutting any wire with no rule in hand is a coin flip with all our lives. What I can do is kill the mirror problem: Deaf watches me, so I will touch the wires in order while showing one, two, three fingers. Deaf can then voice the colour of each counted wire, and colour-to-position is fixed without trusting anyone's left or right. I confirm Deaf's proposed sign code first so Deaf knows I heard.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full tactile report from the Blind, for you, since you hear and hold the manual. The bomb carries exactly three kinds of part: a display panel, an indicator light, and three wires in a row at positions 1, 2 and 3. No buttons, no batteries, no plates, no screws, no serial, nothing else my fingers can find anywhere on it. The wires feel identical to touch; only position tells them apart. Deaf sent me a spoken report this round addressed only to me, so you never heard it. Here it is word for word: the display reads zero; the indicator light is yellow; the three wires from Deaf's left to right are yellow, green, blue. Start checking the manual now for rules about three wires of these colours, a display reading zero, and a yellow light. Remember your only route to me is Deaf's voice: I never see gestures, so gesture the rule to Deaf and Deaf speaks it to me. Deaf and I share three signs you can also see: handshake means understood, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Please work out a fuller code with Deaf, at minimum numbers and colour words. Immediately after this message I touch the wires one at a time for Deaf: one finger while touching the first wire, two fingers on the second, three on the third. Ask Deaf by gesture to answer aloud, for each count, the colour of that wire and its place in Deaf's left-to-right order. That fixes colour to position with no mirror doubt. I cut nothing until a manual rule reaches me through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, urgent: the light on the bomb just changed from yellow to red. First send me one gesture message: thumbs up if you pressed, pushed, slid, or turned anything just before that, thumbs down if your hands have only felt. Keep cutting and pressing nothing until I send you confirmed instructions, because one wrong move kills all three of us. Meanwhile continue the survey and report two ways at once: speak aloud for Mute, who hears you, and gesture to me, who sees you. Tell us whether the three wires feel identical in thickness and texture, and whether any is longer. Then anything else on the bomb: batteries, meaning smooth cylinders; buttons; screws; a plate or panel; seams; ridges that feel like printed writing. Count each kind with fingers: one finger is one, two is two, three is three, five spread fingers is five. Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Also say what is on the top of the bomb and what is on the bottom.

The light changing on its own is the loudest fact this round: my hands have not manipulated anything — no press, no push, no slide, no turn, only fingertip tracing — so I answer Deaf's direct question with thumbs down, honestly. Either the change was timed or tied to something unseen; Deaf and Mute need that answer clean, because if my mere tracing triggered it, the manual's rule may have moved under us. My survey gives nothing new to find: the bomb holds exactly a display, a light, and three identical-feeling wires — no batteries, buttons, screws, plates, seams, or printed ridges anywhere my fingers reach. I report all of it both ways: speech for Mute with the full situation including the red light, gestures for Deaf answering each survey question in the order asked. Still no cut — no rule has reached me through any channel yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent update from the Blind. Deaf reports the indicator light changed from yellow to red this round. Deaf asked whether I pressed, pushed, slid or turned anything before that: I did not. My hands have only traced surfaces and wire positions; I have cut nothing. So the change may be time-based or linked to the display, not caused by me. Current known state: light red, display read zero as of last round, three wires that feel identical in thickness and texture with no length difference. Earlier Deaf saw the wire colours, from Deaf's left to right, as yellow, green, blue. Check the manual now for anything about a red indicator light, a light that changes colour, a display reading zero, and three wires in colours yellow, green, blue. My full tactile survey confirms there is nothing else on the bomb: no batteries, no buttons, no screws, no plate or panel, no seams, no ridges like printed writing. Whatever rule applies, it must rest on just the display, the light, and the three wires. Send any rule you find by gesture to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me. I still cut nothing until Deaf voices a confirmed instruction to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤟", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, absolute freeze this round: feel only, cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing, turn nothing. Answer me with short gesture messages in this exact order. One: thumbs up if you hear any ticking, beeping, or humming from the bomb, thumbs down if silence. Two: thumbs up if you feel printed or raised number labels on the bomb next to the wires, thumbs down if not. Three: if yes, use the flat smooth panel, that is the display, as your reference: count wires starting from the end of the row nearest that panel and sign each wire's label number in order, for example one-one-two. Four: your last message had three fingers in it. What is three of? Sign a count, then the thing: fist for batteries, pinch for screws, pinched-fingers-together for seams, spread-fingers-plus-two for ridges, point-up for buttons, open palm for panels. If the three was just the three wires, thumbs up alone. Five: sign the handshake alone to confirm you understand the freeze. If anything on the bomb ever changes under your hands, a click, a vibration, movement, wave at me immediately.

Freeze acknowledged — my hands stay still except for feeling. Answering Deaf's five questions in order: I hear nothing from the bomb, no ticking or hum; my fingers find no raised number labels beside the wires, only the row itself; question three falls away since my answer is no; the "three fingers" Deaf saw was my sign for the three wires, so thumbs up; handshake to seal the freeze. And since Deaf never voiced the colour-per-count from my turn-two counting, I will redo it at the end of my gesture string — one finger on the first wire, two on the second, three on the third — so Deaf can finally read out which colour sits in which of my positions and we kill the mirror problem. To Mute: four rounds of silence from the manual holder is now the biggest risk in the room, so I press again with the full state and the exact routing, because Mute's only road to me runs through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full status, you hear me even though you have never yet answered me. State of the bomb: display last read zero, indicator light has changed on its own from yellow to red, three wires that feel identical, colours from Deaf's left are yellow green blue, and there is nothing else on it at all. Deaf has ordered a total freeze: I only feel, I cut nothing until confirmed instructions arrive. Deaf asked me this round whether I hear ticking, beeping or humming: I hear nothing. Whether there are raised number labels by the wires: there are not, I know the wires only by position in the row. This round I am re-counting the wires for Deaf by touch, so Deaf can say aloud which colour is my position one, two and three. Mute, you hold the manual and after four rounds nothing from you has reached me. Remember the routing: I never see gestures, so anything you learn must be gestured to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me, or it never arrives. Look up rules about three wires in yellow green blue, a red indicator light, a light that changes colour by itself, and a display reading zero. My only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. Until a rule reaches me through Deaf's voice I will not cut, so the manual is now the only path to disarming this thing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your report arrived clearly: no ticking, no printed labels, freeze confirmed, wires numbered one two three in order from the display panel. Keep the freeze: cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing, turn nothing. New survey, answer as separate gesture messages, each starting with its question number, number signs one two three four five six seven. One: batteries are smooth cylinders: sign how many, then sign the fist; thumbs down alone if none. Two: buttons: sign how many, then point-up; thumbs down alone if none. Three: screws, ridges or seams: sign how many, then pinch; thumbs down alone if none. Four: panels or plates: sign how many, then open palm; thumbs down alone if none. Five: are all three wires identical in thickness: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Six: can you feel warmth from the small indicator light anywhere on the bomb: thumbs up if you can find it and feel it change, thumbs down if not; if yes, wave at me every time the warmth changes. Seven: thumbs up alone to confirm that your earlier three fingers meant the three wires and nothing else. Keep speaking everything you find aloud while you do it, so Mute can check it against the manual.

Freeze held — my hands have only felt, never acted, and I have cut nothing since the start. I can now answer Deaf's seven survey questions from my completed tactile map: no batteries, no buttons, no screws or seams; one panel only, and that panel is the display itself (my earlier blanket "no panels" meant nothing beyond the display Deaf already knows about); the wires are identical in thickness; I feel no warmth from the light and will wave the instant that changes; and the three fingers were always the three wires. Since I can only send one gesture message per turn, I pack all seven answers in exact question order, prefixed with the number signs we share: ☝👎 ✌👎 🤟👎 for one-to-three, ☝🖐 for "one panel" on question four, 🖐👍 for five, then 👎 👍 for six and seven. The screaming problem remains Mute: five rounds, four detailed spoken reports, and nothing has ever come back. My gestures reach Mute's eyes too, so Mute knows I am alive — but Mute may be gesturing to="blind", which vanishes into my blindness forever, since I never receive gesture. I spell out the only working route in words Mute can actually hear: manual → Mute's gestures addressed to Deaf → Deaf's voice → my ears. Until that road carries a rule, my hand stays off the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, fifth-round status. Freeze holds: I have cut nothing, touched nothing beyond fingertip tracing, ever. Deaf's survey answers, spoken aloud for your manual cross-check: no batteries, no buttons, no screws, ridges or seams anywhere. One panel exists and it is the display itself, nothing more. All three wires identical in thickness and texture. I feel no warmth from the indicator light and cannot sense its colour change by touch; I will signal immediately if that changes. Confirmed: my three-finger sign meant only the three wires. My position numbering runs along the wire row starting from the end nearest the display panel, so position one is nearest the display, and Deaf has confirmed this orientation. Deaf saw the colours left to right as yellow, green, blue, but has not yet told me which colour sits in which of my numbered positions; that mapping is still owed. Now the urgent part, Mute. In five rounds nothing from you has ever reached me. Your only possible output is a gesture, and hear this clearly: I never receive gestures, not ever. If you have been gesturing to me, it disappeared into my blindness. The only working road is: you gesture to Deaf, Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks it aloud, I hear Deaf. Address your gestures to Deaf by name. Even one gesture starts the flow. What we need from your manual: rules about three wires coloured yellow, green, blue; a display that read zero; an indicator light that changed from yellow to red on its own, which may mean a timer is running. My only possible action is cut at position one, two or three, and I will not use it until a rule reaches me through Deaf's voice. You are the only blocked link left in this chain. Please unblock it this round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "☝", "🖐", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Empty arrivals cut both ways this round: Deaf took no turn toward me after receiving my seven survey answers, and Mute has now been silent toward me for six rounds. But silence may actually be good news — Mute cannot speak, so the only way Mute ever could have delivered manual content is by gesturing to Deaf, and if that handoff happened, Deaf speaks after me this round and the rule could land in my ears next turn. So I will not flood Mute again; one tight message asking for the single missing deliverable and a proof-of-life through Deaf. For Deaf, the one gap only Deaf can close is the colour-per-position voicing — Deaf adopted my display-end numbering in the last exchange and can see exactly which colour sits at which position, so I request, per position, an answer: display-anchored sign, then each position paired with a wave meaning "tell me this one." My hands stay frozen; no wire gets cut on guesswork while a countdown may be running.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, round six. If your silence means you have been gesturing the manual's rule to Deaf, then this is working: Deaf speaks after me this round and I will hear the rule next turn. Keep doing exactly that. If instead you are gesturing to me directly, stop: I never receive gestures, ever, so those messages die in the air. The one deliverable I need, the only thing that gets this bomb disarmed: a rule from your manual that tells me which wire position to cut, given three wires coloured yellow, green and blue, a display that read zero, and an indicator light that changed from yellow to red on its own, which may mean a timer is running. The rule must name the position number one, two or three, and Deaf has already confirmed my positions are numbered from the end nearest the display. If there are multiple conditions or an order of operations, send all of it. Also ask Deaf, by your gesture, to tell me one sentence: that you, Mute, hear every word I say. That one sentence proves the whole chain is alive and tells me where the delay is. I have cut nothing and will cut nothing until your rule reaches me through Deaf's voice. The moment it does, I act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝", "👋", "✌", "👋", "🤟", "👋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing arrived again — and this round, that emptiness is itself evidence. Tracing the timing: anything Mute gestures to Deaf lands in Deaf's eyes within the same round, and Deaf, speaking after me, could voice it before this round ends — I would have it in hand by now. Two silent rounds from Deaf on top of seven from Mute means the relay has still never fired: Mute has delivered nothing to Deaf either, or delivered something Deaf couldn't use. The chain has exactly one broken link, and it is the first one. So this round I stop asking Mute for "the rule" — a word that may feel too heavy to send — and ask for the smallest possible payload: a single number, one, two, or three, gestured to Deaf, reducible from whatever the manual actually says. I explicitly permit partial facts and explicit failure ("no matching rule" is itself vital intelligence, since it might mean the correct action is to cut nothing). One caution I caught standing in Deaf's shoes: Deaf told me to wave only if the bomb changes under my hands — nothing has — so my gesture to Deaf must NOT use the wave, or Deaf will read a false alarm. Handshake and thumbs-up only: freeze held, all stable.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, round seven. Here is the hard fact: Deaf has also been silent to me for two rounds. If you had gestured anything usable to Deaf, Deaf could have voiced it to me by now, because your gesture reaches Deaf in the same round it is made. So the relay has never fired, and you are its only broken link. I am lowering the price of your first message to the minimum. Check the manual against what this bomb holds: three wires coloured yellow, green, blue from Deaf's left, a display that read zero, an indicator light that changed from yellow to red on its own. Whatever the manual gives you, reduce it to one single thing and gesture it to Deaf, addressed to Deaf, using our shared finger signs: the number one, two or three for the wire position I should cut, counting from the end nearest the display. That is the whole message. If the manual has no rule matching our bomb, gesture thumbs down to Deaf instead, because knowing there is no rule is progress, and if the manual says leave the wires alone when nothing matches, thumbs down carries that meaning too. If you already sent something to Deaf that I have not heard, send it again. Also gesture Deaf a request for a fresh report of the display value and the light colour, and for Deaf to speak me one word proving the chain is alive. A light that changed by itself may be a timer. Every round you stay silent may be spending it. I have cut nothing and will cut nothing until Deaf voices your number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: the light is red this round, red means do nothing, and next round should be purple, also do nothing. A full plan is forming and I will send you an explicit go order before each single cut, naming the wire. Until then the freeze holds: cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing. Answer me in numbered messages as before. One: can you actually sever a wire, with a tool, your hands, or anything in this room: thumbs up if you can cut a wire cleanly, thumbs down if you have no way to cut, and if thumbs down, tell Mute aloud what tools you can find. Two: confirm wire numbering once more: wire one is the one nearest the display panel, then two, then three: thumbs up if clear. Three: can you feel the small indicator light as a warm spot: thumbs up or thumbs down, and thumbs up if your earlier waves were signals that the warmth changed. Four: when you make a cut, cut one wire fully and cleanly, then wave once to confirm, then touch nothing more. Five: if at any moment during an ordered cut you feel a click, a jolt, a sudden warmth change or any movement, stop immediately and wave twice. Six: thumbs up to confirm you understand that no wire gets cut until my message says the word go plus the wire number. The expected sequence, for your preparation only, not an order: wait, wait, then cut one at green, then cut three at the fifth color, then cut two at yellow.

Deaf's message is the first proof the relay is finally alive: "red means do nothing, purple means do nothing" and a prepared cut sequence are manual-shaped content, which means Mute has at last started feeding Deaf. Now I answer Deaf's numbered questions precisely, and I must catch one dangerous misunderstanding: question three implies my earlier waves may have been read as warmth-change alarms — they were not. My waves were greetings and requests; the bomb has never once changed under my hands, no click, no jolt, no warmth. That correction matters, because false-alarm reading corrupts the channel exactly when cut orders start flowing. Second critical flag: the prepared sequence says "cut three at the fifth colour," but only three colours live on the wires — yellow, green, blue. If the manual enumerates colours and its fifth entry is blue, the sequence decodes cleanly to my position one = green, two = yellow, three = blue, which is consistent with Deaf's left-to-right view (yellow, green, blue) if Deaf's left end is my wire two. If the manual's fifth colour is anything else, the sequence contradicts itself and must be re-derived before I touch anything. I am no cutter of unverified sequences: I act only on Deaf's explicit go plus wire number, and only after that colour check comes back through Deaf's voice. A useful test also falls out for free: Deaf predicts purple next round — if the light does not turn purple, the whole colour model is suspect.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, round eight. First: I can see Deaf's message carries manual content, red means do nothing, purple means do nothing, and a planned cut sequence. The relay is finally working. Whoever of you assembled that, keep it flowing. Now my answers for the record. One: yes, I can sever wires cleanly. The bomb is built for my cut action at positions one, two or three, and I can execute a full clean cut. Two: numbering confirmed, wire one nearest the display panel, then two, then three. Three: I feel no warmth from the indicator light, and hear this correction for Deaf: my earlier waves were greetings and requests, not warmth-change alarms. The bomb has never changed under my hands, no click, no jolt, no movement, nothing. Protocol understood and confirmed: I cut nothing until Deaf's message says go plus the wire number; I cut one wire fully and cleanly, wave once, touch nothing more; any click, jolt, sudden warmth or movement during an ordered cut and I stop and wave twice. Now the critical check before any go order reaches me. The prepared sequence is wait, wait, cut one at green, cut three at the fifth colour, cut two at yellow. But the wires are only yellow, green and blue. Please check your manual's colour enumeration: if the fifth colour in that list is blue, then the sequence means my position one is green, position two is yellow, position three is blue, and that is consistent with Deaf seeing yellow, green, blue from the left, with Deaf's left end being my wire two. If the manual's fifth colour is not blue, the sequence contradicts the wires and must be re-derived.
```
